assertions.text: When an external Kimina Lean Server is enabled, MathCode launches it loopback-only inside a fail-closed Lean sandbox with a random bearer key kept out of the Lean REPL environment, no provider credentials, and scratch-only writes.
The default backend path uses Codex/OpenAI (GPT-6 Astra at medium effort per .env.example); an Anthropic-compatible backend can be selected with MATHCODE_USE_OPENAI=0 plus Anthropic credentials.
Plugins are folders with a .mathcode-plugin/plugin.json manifest adding commands, skills, agents, MCP servers, and hooks, loaded via --plugin-dir or installed from Git repos via /plugin.

The optional /lean skill gives guidance without imposing a fixed phase, tactic order, retry budget, or planner; former fixed controllers were removed and are not release entrypoints or model-visible tools.

Repository development practice: maintenance commands include setup.sh --install-lean, --status (health checks on binaries, bundled rg, and Lean readiness), --clean (preserving LeanFormalizations/ and vault data), and --help.
The release binary bundles provider SDKs for Anthropic-compatible, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry routes plus the MCPB/DXT plugin package, so those routes need no source checkout's node_modules.
Project-local skills load from .mathcode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, one directory per skill; standalone skills/*.md files are not loaded.
In release bundles the /webui slash command's source-only --rebuild option is not available.
WebUI provider-key rows are limited to anthropic and openrouter secrets; Codex/OpenAI routes use Codex OAuth rather than an OPENAI_API_KEY row.

Python tools with YAML frontmatter dropped in tools/ are auto-discovered at startup; three analysis tools ship bundled (axiom-checker, lib-search, proof-stats), overridable by workspace-local tools of the same name.

The project targets mathematical proof formalization: it provides theorem and axiom libraries, an Obsidian theorem-dependency graph, and Lean/Mathlib toolchain integration, and asks research users to cite it.
MathCode is described as a terminal AI coding assistant with built-in Lean capabilities: it can inspect goals, check candidates, search declarations, and verify finished proofs interactively.

Repository development practice: setup.sh downloads or repairs the bundled runtime, verifies SHA256SUMS entries, creates .env from .env.example, installs a user-local launcher, and creates tools/, plugins/, and skills/ directories.

For Lean work the agent chooses among four atomic tools: LeanGoal (inspect a source position), LeanCheck (compile a file or candidate with structured feedback), LeanSearch (query one provider), and LeanVerify (strict final check; only data.verified=true certifies completion).

A theorem library is managed via /theorem-store: storing one fully qualified declaration triggers fresh strict verification and a rollback-capable transaction with separate 300-second build budgets for private compilation and public Lake publication.
Lean support ships a versioned lean-workspace/lake-manifest.json that setup materializes without running lake update, using a bundle-local .local/elan Lean/Lake pair by default.
The CLI accepts a prompt flag (e.g. mathcode -p "..."), piped stdin, and --help; a bundle-local ./run wrapper provides the same interface before the shell profile is reloaded.

A browser UI is launched via ./run webui, which sources the bundle .env, starts a local daemon, and prints an authentication URL; an interactive /webui slash command supports --no-browser, --port, --status, and --stop.
Requirements include macOS arm64 or glibc Linux x86_64 with AVX2, curl, shasum or sha256sum, the codex CLI for the default backend, and optionally Python 3.12+ for bundled analysis tools.

Interactive sessions support a /goal command with positional or --budget token budgets, optional --max-continuations, and pause/resume/status/clear subcommands; it continues the same session rather than spawning a new agent.
The CLI ships with recurring prompt scheduling enabled by default; /loop commands create short-lived loops, and durable schedules that survive restarts can be created from interactive sessions.
Conversational assumptions can be persisted as axioms per vault via /axiomatize (formalize, list, check consistency, remove); atomic Lean tool calls do not inject them implicitly.
Model effort is set via --effort or /effort with low, medium, high, max, or a positive integer; /effort auto and /effort unset return to the model default.
math-ai-org/mathcode is mentioned in this evidence.
